Employers guide

WIBA insurance in Kenya: an employer guide

Chestnut Insurance Agency editorial team · Published 21 November 2026

WIBA insurance is how an employer insures its liability to compensate employees for work-related injury or disease under the Work Injury Benefits Act. If you employ people in Kenya, you should assume the obligation applies to you and arrange cover that matches your real workforce and payroll.

What WIBA is for

The Act sets out a statutory compensation framework for employees injured at work or suffering occupational disease. The employer carries the liability and is expected to insure it. WIBA insurance transfers that financial obligation to an insurer, within the terms of the policy and the law.

Who counts as an employee

Do not limit the list to permanent staff. Casual, seasonal and contract workers can fall within the definition depending on their working arrangement. When arranging cover, describe your actual workforce, including field staff, drivers and site workers.

How WIBA is usually rated

Accurate payroll matters. Understated figures can create problems at claim stage and when the insurer audits.

  • Annual payroll, often by job category
  • The nature of the work and its risk level
  • Number of employees
  • Claims history

WIBA is not the same as other staff benefits

Group personal accident, group life and medical cover are separate benefits. They can complement WIBA but do not replace it. Employers with hazardous work should also ask whether an employer’s liability extension is available.

Practical checklist

  • Confirm the policy period and renewal date
  • Check that payroll and job categories reflect today’s workforce
  • Know how to notify the insurer of an injury and keep the contact on site
  • Keep injury records and report according to current legal requirements
  • Review cover after hiring surges or new site operations

Check current requirements

Procedures and requirements can change. This guide is general education, not legal advice. Confirm current obligations with the relevant authority and your advisor.

This guide is general education about insurance in Kenya. It is not legal or financial advice and does not describe any specific policy. Policy wording, exclusions and the law that applies at the time govern. Speak to an advisor about your situation.
